One clear path.
From source to restore.

HomeVault Personal is a Go CLI/TUI that orchestrates Restic and rclone. The file-backup MVP has been tested with generated data on Ubuntu, including an encrypted Google Drive round trip and byte-for-byte restore comparison.

01 / SELECT

Your files, on your server

Choose source directories explicitly. Running databases need a consistent export first; automatic database preparation is not implemented yet.

02 / ENCRYPT

A dedicated backup repository

Restic encrypts repository data before upload. You keep the recovery password separately; losing it can mean losing access to the backup.

03 / RECOVER

Restore without replacing the original

Select an explicit snapshot and a separate empty destination. Check the restored files before relying on the backup.

Google Drive storage.
Limited, explicit access.

The personal installation connects to the Google account you authorize. It requests drive.file access for app-created or explicitly authorized files, not unrestricted access to your whole Drive.

Self-hosted, not a central cloud service. OAuth tokens stay in the operator’s private rclone configuration. Backup content goes to the authorized storage account. Google still processes storage metadata and normal service requests.

Built now.
Planned next.

The current version supports file backups, snapshots, metadata checks and guarded restores. The following are roadmap items, not capabilities currently available in the personal installation.

  • Database-aware exports for Docker applicationsPlanned
  • Restore into an isolated stack and verify the applicationPlanned
  • Guided setup, durable job history and failure alertsPlanned

No paid hosting, uptime promise or public backup account service. Keep independent backups and test recovery.
